title: Limitations periods across procedural questions
summary: A limitations period restricts the time for bringing or enforcing a claim. Its procedural treatment can affect jurisdictional strategy, the Erie inquiry, amendment, and the availability of relief.
notes: These cases address different mechanisms. Filing a complaint, serving it, and adding a party can have distinct effects under the governing provisions.

sections.Meaning: A limitations period restricts the time for bringing or enforcing a claim. Its procedural treatment can affect jurisdictional strategy, the Erie inquiry, amendment, and the availability of relief.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the relevant statute, what event commences or preserves the action, and the procedural question before the court. Ragan and Walker address state limitations treatment in federal court; Krupski addresses whether an amendment relates back.
